stories.title: Apollo, UDR Partner on $2B Multifamily Joint Venture
stories.excerpt: Multifamily real estate investment trust (REIT) UDR has partnered with alternative asset manager Apollo Global Management on a $2 billion multifamily joint venture, the firms announced Wednesday. Together, UDR and Apollo will own a portfolio of 19 multifamily communities spanning 7,059 units. UDR will operate and manage the portfolio, while Apollo will invest $1.34 billion of equity capital and acquire a two-thirds interest in the JV. The deal, which was arranged by Citigroup Global Markets and Wells Fargo Securities, is expected to close Oct. 29. “UDR’s partnership with Apollo provides access to a new, low-cost permanent source of equity capital,” Dave Bragg, UDR’s chief financial officer, said in a statement. “We expect the transaction to be accretive to earnings and intend to deploy the proceeds into higher-growth assets and other general corporate purposes.” As part of the structure of the deal, UDR will retain a one-third interest in the JV but will have the option to repurchase Apollo’s interest in five years. The JV is expected to produce a portfolio with an average revenue of $2,058 per home and an age of 39 years. UDR and Apollo did not provide the locations for any of the multifamily communities that are part of the JV. The firms did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. “With this transaction, we believe we will be positioned to take advantage of compelling opportunities in the marketplace, while improving the quality of our wholly owned portfolio and strengthening our balance sheet, all in an accretive manner,” Tom Toomey, chairman, president and CEO of UDR, said in a statement. “Our shareholders will benefit not only from the flexibility to move assets in and out of our newly established joint venture, but also from the ability to realize outsized value creation over time.” Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Apollo invests $1.34B equity, acquires two-thirds stake in UDR's 19-property, 7,059-unit JV.
UDR retains one-third interest, retains management; proceeds fund higher-growth acquisitions.
Deal closes Oct. 29; structured to provide UDR low-cost permanent equity capital.
stories.summary: UDR and Apollo Global Management announced a $2 billion multifamily joint venture covering 19 communities and 7,059 units across unspecified markets. Apollo commits $1.34 billion in equity for a two-thirds ownership stake while UDR operates the portfolio and retains one-third interest plus a repurchase option. UDR CFO noted the partnership provides low-cost permanent capital and expects proceeds to be deployed into higher-growth assets.
stories.impact: This signals UDR's shift from balance-sheet ownership toward capital-light management and selective growth deployment. Institutional alternative asset managers (Apollo) stepping in to buy stabilized portfolios at scale reduces competition for development financing and permits developers to recycle equity into higher-return development or value-add plays; watch for UDR announcements on deployment markets and product types over next 12 months.

stories.title: BridgeCity Capital Lends $36M on Long Island City Condos Build
stories.excerpt: Winspire Development has landed $36.2 million of construction financing to build a condominium project in Long Island City, Queens, Commercial Observer has learned. Brooklyn-based BridgeCity Capital provided the loan for the developer’s planned 41-unit condo building at 10-56 46th Road. The development is a mile southwest of Winspire’s Mason LIC condo project at 40-46 24th Street that debuted in late 2024 and has sold all 42 units. Arrow Real Estate Advisors negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Morris Betesh, Omar Ferreira and Jonah Schultz. “Winspire Development has already shown with Mason LIC that they can deliver a product that resonates with buyers in Long Island City, and this financing positions their next project for continued success,” Betesh, founder and managing partner at Arrow Real Estate Advisors, said in a statement. The 57,670-gross-square-foot 10-56 46th Road project will also include ground-floor retail space. The development, near the corner of 46th Road and 11th Street, is slated for completion in spring 2028. EJ Ehrlich, director of originations at BridgeCity Capital, said in a statement Winspire is a repeat borrower with a “proven track record.” That, “coupled with the continued strength of the LIC market, gives us tremendous confidence in their ability to successfully execute this project,” Ehrlich said. Winspire Development did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BridgeCity Capital lends $36.2M construction on Winspire's 41-unit LIC condo project.
Winspire's prior 42-unit Mason LIC condo sold out in late 2024; proves demand.
Long Island City sees repeated condo development capital, signaling buyer confidence.
stories.summary: Winspire Development secured $36.2 million in construction financing from Brooklyn-based BridgeCity Capital for a 41-unit condominium at 10-56 46th Road in Long Island City, Queens. The developer's previous 42-unit Mason LIC condo project at nearby 40-46 24th Street achieved full sellout after launching in late 2024. Arrow Real Estate Advisors brokered the debt, noting the proven buyer appetite for the product and location.
stories.impact: Rapid repeat financing and full sellout of prior phase demonstrate sustained condo demand in LIC; signals capital is flowing to for-sale product over rentals in this submarket. Developers should monitor conversion opportunities and condo absorption in LIC—low inventory of new supply and strong sales velocity may support density and pricing that favor vertical product over rental communities in this specific Queens corridor.

stories.title: The Robots Are Coming, and Other AI-Related Observations From the Experts
stories.excerpt: Isaac Asimov saw this coming. Commercial Observer’s Power Tech & AI Forum and Reception at Marx Realty’s 10 Grand Central on Oct. 19 featured in-depth discussions about the latest in AI from real estate technology insiders. A little bit into it, Abhinav “Abe” Somani, founder of Cadastral and head of real estate for Legora, answered a question about what’s coming for AI in 2027 with an answer right out of “Blade Runner.” “For real estate in particular, the big shock is going to be the humanoid robots that will start getting released next year,” Somani said casually. “That is really going to change everything we’ve done. From 2D text-based AI to 3D vision, voice and sensory details, this has more long-term implications for real estate than producing a legal bill.” The event was emceed by Commercial Observer Deputy Editor Tom Acitelli, who greeted attendees — including honorees on CO’s annual power tech list — with a quick but powerful reminder of the import and impact of the current artificial intelligence revolution. “In my tenure covering real estate, I’ve watched dozens of technologies arrive on the scene and promise to shake up the business,” said Acitelli. “Some have done just that. Others, like the Metaverse, never found their footing. But I don’t think any have brought the full scope of upheaval and disruption that AI has.” Continuing on this theme, the evening’s first panel, titled Empowering Deal Acceleration: Inside The Tech-Enabled Transactions Shaping Today’s Market, included comments from Somani; Zach Aarons, co-founder and general partner at MetaProp; Nick Durst, principal and director of operations at the Durst Organization; Joseph Sipala, managing director at JLL; and moderator Cher Chang, founder and CEO of Literock Capital and partner and head of capital markets at JLJ Capital. stories.title: Venu Closes $60M Sale-Leaseback on McKinney Amphitheater
stories.excerpt: Venu Holding Corporation closed a $60 million sale-leaseback transaction on the land beneath its Sunset Amphitheater and adjacent parking garage in McKinney, Texas. The transaction was completed with STORE Capital, a real estate investment trust. Sunset Amphitheater at McKinney, a 20,000-capacity, multi-season venue serving the Dallas-Fort Worth market, is expected to open in the first quarter of 2027. Proceeds from the sale-leaseback are expected to be used to repay the Company’s approximately $20 million bridge financing from Ryan, and to fund the completion of construction of Sunset Amphitheater at McKinney. VENU currently operates venues in Colorado Springs, Colorado, and Gainesville, Georgia, with projects under development in Broken Arrow, Oklahoma; Houston, Frisco, and El Paso, Texas; and Chattanooga, Tennessee; and has a national footprint that continues to grow. VENU is powered by a differentiated financing approach that combines fractional ownership, public-private partnerships, sale-leaseback structures, and C-PACE financing to enable capital-efficient expansion across underserved markets. bullets: Venu closes $60M sale-leaseback with STORE Capital on Sunset Amphitheater land in McKinney.
20,000-capacity venue opening Q1 2027; proceeds repay $20M bridge, fund construction.
McKinney, Texas part of expanding VENU footprint; Dallas-Fort Worth entertainment/hospitality growth.
stories.summary: Venu Holding Corporation closed a $60 million sale-leaseback transaction with STORE Capital on the land and parking garage beneath its forthcoming Sunset Amphitheater in McKinney, Texas. The 20,000-capacity multi-season venue is expected to open in Q1 2027 and will serve the Dallas-Fort Worth market. Proceeds will repay a $20 million bridge loan and complete construction.
stories.impact: McKinney continues to emerge as entertainment/hospitality hub within DFW; large-capacity venue signals population density and spending power in outer suburbs. Multifamily developers should note McKinney as high-growth submarket with infrastructure investment and entertainment amenities—potential anchor for mixed-use or near-venue residential development to capture event-driven and relocated workforce demand.

stories.title: Brooklyn Surpasses Manhattan in Multifamily Sales in Q3: Report
stories.excerpt: Sales of apartment buildings and other multifamily properties across New York City — specifically Manhattan, the Bronx, Queens and Brooklyn — during the first three quarters of 2026 grew on a year-over-year basis, with Brooklyn coming out on top in the third quarter, according to the latest multifamily quarterly report from Ariel Property Advisors. Brooklyn saw the most multifamily activity in July, August and September with $693.8 million in total dollar volume, although that was a 12.8 percent decline from 2025’s third quarter, Ariel found. Brooklyn’s transaction volume also increased 12.7 percent in this year’s third quarter year-over-year to 178 sales. Meanwhile, dollar volume in Manhattan — below 96th street — declined 43.6 percent year-over-year to $685.2 million, according to Ariel. Transactions in the borough increased 1.8 percent to 58 for the third quarter. Upper Manhattan’s dollar volume — above 96th Street — grew by 32.8 percent on a year-over-year basis, while transactions declined 5.9 percent from the same quarter a year ago to 16. Overall in the four boroughs that Ariel tracked, multifamily sales totaled $6.99 billion through 1,044 transactions in the first three quarters of 2026, representing yearly increases of 7.9 percent and 11.5 percent, respectively. However, overall dollar volume for the third quarter declined by 23.3 percent year-over-year to $1.84 billion, the Ariel data found. During the third quarter, there were four transactions of $50 million or more that totaled $388.7 million, which is a decline from eight deals of that kind in the third quarter of 2025, which totaled $999.2 million. Across the markets Ariel surveyed, properties that have 75 percent or more free-market units accounted for 63.1 percent of the third quarter’s dollar volume, while buildings with 75 percent or more rent-stabilized units held 19.2 percent of the market. bullets: Brooklyn Q3 2024 sales: $693.8M (178 units), exceeds Manhattan's $685.2M (58 units).

stories.summary: Brooklyn surpassed Manhattan in multifamily sales volume during Q3 2024, with $693.8 million in dollar volume across 178 sales versus Manhattan's $685.2 million across 58 transactions, according to Ariel Property Advisors. Brooklyn's dollar volume declined 12.8% year-over-year while Manhattan fell 43.6%. Upper Manhattan (above 96th St.) grew 32.8% YoY but represented only 16 transactions.
stories.impact: Capital rotation out of core Manhattan and into outer boroughs (Brooklyn) and northern submarket reveals limited investor appetite for trophy Manhattan assets; signals continued cap rate compression in Brooklyn as competition for stable, value-add assets intensifies. Developers should prioritize Brooklyn acquisitions and development pipelines now while pricing reflects re-allocation; expect cap rates to firm in Manhattan as investors seek alternatives, potentially freezing newer development starts there.

stories.title: Affinius Capital Provides $94M Refi for Dallas-Area Industrial Property
stories.excerpt: Hillwood, a real estate firm founded by former Independent presidential candidate Ross Perot, has secured a $94 million loan to refinance an industrial property in the Dallas-Fort Worth region, Commercial Observer can first report Affinius Capital supplied the loan for three warehouse facilities encompassing 1.2 million square feet at Crossroads Logistics Park in Midlothian, Texas. Proceeds from the loan will be used to facilitate continued lease-up of the property, comprising Buildings 1, 2 and 4, that were built in 2023. “Based on our experience in the industrial sector, Crossroads Logistics Park offers the scale, functionality and connectivity that today’s industrial users require in what we believe is one of the country’s most important distribution markets,” Costa Kontoulis, managing director at Affinius Capital, said in a statement. “With three newly built facilities and strong access across the Dallas-Fort Worth region, we see a compelling opportunity to support Hillwood as it advances the property through lease-up and stabilization.” JLL arranged the transaction with a capital markets team consisting of Trey Morsbach, John Rose, Jarrod McCabe, Ryan Pollack, Chad Lisbeth and Scott Harbert. Located at 1011 John Clark Road, 28 miles southwest of Downtown Dallas, Crossroads Logistics Park benefits as an industrial property from its access to major highways including Interstate 20 and Interstate 35, according to Affinius. It is also 33 miles south of Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport. Hillwood did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Affinius Capital refinances $94M on Hillwood's 1.2M SF Crossroads Logistics Park (DFW).
Three newly built warehouse facilities (2023); in lease-up phase in Midlothian, Texas.
Reflects continued DFW industrial strength and lender confidence in lease-up dynamics.
stories.summary: Hillwood, the real estate firm founded by Ross Perot, secured a $94 million refinance from Affinius Capital for three warehouse buildings totaling 1.2 million square feet at Crossroads Logistics Park in Midlothian, Texas. The facilities were built in 2023 and are currently in lease-up. Proceeds support continued leasing and stabilization.
stories.impact: Industrial refinancing in DFW signals strong underlying logistics demand and lender confidence in lease-up trajectories; not directly relevant to multifamily but indicates robust regional economic fundamentals and employer/distribution network expansion driving population and wage growth. Monitor DFW multifamily absorption and rent growth as industrial expansion supports job growth and in-migration.

stories.title: Agador Spartacus Inks $58.5M Loan to Build Two Deltona BTR Communities
stories.excerpt: Agador Spartacus closed on a $58.5 million construction loan for two build-to-rent communities in Deltona, Florida. Anchor Loans provided the loan. The financings include approximately $30.2 million for Magnolia Cottages at Deltona, a 153-home community, and $28.3 million for Magnolia Villas at Deltona, a 126-home community. Located on adjacent parcels, the projects will add a combined 279 rental homes, including a mix of cottages, duplexes and townhomes. Both communities are planned with dog parks and clubhouse amenities. Located between Orlando and Daytona Beach, the communities offer convenient access to major employment centers across Central Florida, including the nearby Howland Job Zone, home to healthcare, logistics and retail employers. Anchor has previously financed Agador projects including Magnolia at Lake Hamilton, a $35.4 million multifamily financing in Winter Haven, and Lake Ella Estates, a $36.8 million financing for a 132-home build-to-rent community in Lady Lake. bullets: Agador Spartacus closes $58.5M construction loan for two build-to-rent communities in Deltona, FL.
Combined 279 rental homes (cottages, duplexes, townhomes); Magnolia Cottages (153 units), Magnolia Villas (126 units).

stories.summary: Agador Spartacus closed a $58.5 million construction loan from Anchor Loans for two build-to-rent communities in Deltona, Florida: Magnolia Cottages (153 homes, $30.2M) and Magnolia Villas (126 homes, $28.3M). The communities feature cottage, duplex, and townhome products with dog parks and clubhouses, positioned between Orlando and Daytona near the Howland Job Zone's healthcare, logistics, and retail employers.
stories.impact: Deltona BTR financing signals capital flowing to secondary Florida markets with growing employment anchors (healthcare/logistics); Central Florida's job growth and housing shortage support rent and absorption in non-prime submarkets. Developers should monitor Howland Job Zone expansion and track Deltona's rent growth relative to Orlando metro—secondary submarkets with employment clusters often deliver outsized returns early in development cycle before investor capital saturates supply.

stories.title: Appian Investments Acquires 19-Story Greenboro Office Tower
stories.excerpt: Appian Investments acquired the Renaissance Plaza in Greensboro. The 287,000-square-foot office tower was purchased for $22 million. CBRE’s Patrick Gildea, Matt Smith and Greg Wilson represented the seller, Richardson Properties, in the transaction. Renaissance Plaza is a 19-story office tower located at the corner of North Elm Street and Abe Brenner Place in the heart of downtown Greensboro. Delivered in 1990, the property features a two-story atrium lobby, an attached six-level parking deck with 300 spaces, an on-site cafe and floor-to-ceiling glass overlooking the city’s central business district. Richardson Properties completed nearly $4 million in capital improvements in 2023, including renovations to the lobby and common areas, elevator upgrades and enhancements to key building systems. The property is anchored by a roster of longstanding tenants spanning the financial services and legal sectors, including Arch Mortgage Insurance, Brooks Pierce, Fox Rothschild, Schell Bray and RSM US. The post Appian Investments Acquires 19-Story Greenboro Office Tower appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Appian Investments acquires Renaissance Plaza office tower, Greensboro, for $22M.
19-story, 287K SF class-A office built 1990; financial services/legal tenant roster; down-town location.
Office asset acquisition, not multifamily; minimal direct relevance to residential development.
stories.summary: Appian Investments purchased Renaissance Plaza, a 19-story, 287,000-square-foot office tower in downtown Greensboro, North Carolina, for $22 million from Richardson Properties. The 1990-vintage property features institutional tenants in financial services and law and had received approximately $4 million in capital improvements in 2023. The acquisition represents a distressed or value-play office purchase.
stories.impact: No direct impact to multifamily development. Office distress in secondary markets (Greensboro) may signal opportunity for conversion to residential or mixed-use on long-term hold, but current transaction is straight office repositioning; track Greensboro office-to-residential conversion potential if cap rates remain elevated.

stories.title: Bond Market’s AI Warning Is About Growth, Not Prices
stories.excerpt: Executive Summary The bond market delivered a warning last week: Concern about an artificial intelligence debt bust can outweigh inflation anxiety, at least temporarily. Investors sought safety in U.S. Treasurys as AI-linked credit sold off, pushing government yields lower despite stronger-than-expected inflation readings. The move revived an argument that an AI credit unwind could become deflationary. The evidence supports a narrower conclusion. Financing stress presents a potential drag on investment and demand, but market pricing has not established that investors expect falling economywide prices. CoreWeave Becomes the Epicenter CoreWeave, the AI cloud provider that has borrowed heavily to build data centers, became the epicenter. Its five-year credit default swaps traded past 1,100 basis points, implying roughly a 64% chance of default within five years, up from about 30% a year ago. Cash bonds showed pressure as well. CoreWeave’s 9.625% notes due 2032 traded at $0.79 on the dollar, illustrating the financing exposure behind its infrastructure expansion; its bond yield reached approximately 16% before retreating toward 14%. The stress climbed the quality ladder. Oracle’s swaps approached 300 basis points. SoftBank’s widened 24 basis points in a single day to 424. Default protection on Amazon, Alphabet and Meta also hit record levels, though far below the weaker names. It also highlights why lower Treasury yields do not necessarily relieve stressed borrowers. A declining government benchmark can be overwhelmed by a widening corporate credit spread, leaving the company’s overall borrowing cost higher. The pain is concentrated, however. Dollar high-yield AI-related spreads widened 25 basis points in one day to a record 360 basis points over Treasurys, while non-AI spreads moved just two basis points and remained below their March peak. What is being repriced is a debt-funded buildout. The five largest hyperscalers issued $121 billion in U.S. corporate bonds in 202
bullets: AI credit stress widening: CoreWeave CDS >1,100 bps, bonds trading $0.79 on dollar.
Oracle, SoftBank, Amazon credit also under pressure; bond market signals financing risk.
AI infrastructure debt unwind presents potential deflationary drag on investment and demand.
stories.summary: The bond market signaled concern about an AI credit bubble unwind amid weakness in CoreWeave, an AI cloud infrastructure provider. CoreWeave's five-year CDS traded above 1,100 basis points (implying ~64% default probability) while its 2032 bonds traded at $0.79 on the dollar with yields near 14–16%. Stress climbed the quality ladder to Oracle, SoftBank, and Amazon as investors rotated to safety.
stories.impact: AI infrastructure financing stress may reduce development and capex-driven demand if credit markets tighten further and borrowing costs for AI-heavy employers spike; watch for tech sector hiring freezes or layoffs that would suppress multifamily demand in tech hubs (Austin, Seattle, Bay Area). Conversely, if AI credit unwind triggers broader growth concerns, the Fed may cut rates—potentially improving multifamily debt structures and refinance prospects.

stories.title: Newmark Affiliate Arranges $369M Financing for 11 Florida Affordable Housing Properties
stories.excerpt: Newmark Group arranged a $369 million Fannie Mae credit facility on behalf of April Housing, supporting the long-term preservation of an 11-property affordable housing portfolio located throughout Florida. The financing consisted of a $221.4 million fixed-rate draw and a $147.6 million floating-rate draw, structured as an interest-only facility through Fannie Mae. A buydown on the fixed-rate portion of the facility helped maximize proceeds and support the overall financing strategy. Newmark’s Evan Williams arranged the financing on behalf of April Housing, with Director Ian McIntire, Seante Vang and Nicole Phillips also supporting the assignment. The transaction presented several complexities, including the review and analysis of 24 separate regulatory agreements across 11 properties. April Housing, a Blackstone portfolio company, is a provider of solutions and capital to create and preserve high-quality affordable housing throughout the United States. The company oversees one of the nation’s largest portfolios of LIHTC (Low-Income Housing Tax Credit) housing. bullets: Newmark arranges $369M Fannie Mae credit facility for April Housing (Blackstone portfolio).

stories.summary: Newmark Group arranged a $369 million Fannie Mae credit facility on behalf of April Housing (a Blackstone company) to support long-term preservation of 11 affordable housing properties across Florida. The financing comprised $221.4 million in fixed-rate and $147.6 million in floating-rate tranches structured as interest-only through Fannie Mae, with a buydown on the fixed portion to maximize proceeds.
stories.impact: Fannie Mae capital flowing into LIHTC preservation signals government priority on affordable housing; developers should note Fannie Mae appetite for seasoned affordable portfolios as a stable exit or hold-to-maturity strategy. LIHTC cap rates and Fannie Mae pricing on affordable assets may compress further if government support continues, making new-build affordable development less competitive on returns relative to for-profit multifamily in same markets.
